FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment` freezes the initial model specs in `_models` during `assign()` and `reassign()` later scores only against that frozen list, not against the manager’s live-updated fingerprints. See [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L495), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L519), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L536), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3742), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3880). The result is that allocation can use observed performance, but role reassignment cannot; COL/PAR role changes remain anchored to initialization-time fingerprints.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change `reassign()` to accept the current live `ModelSpec` set or a fingerprint lookup, and refresh `capability_scores` from that same live source before computing new roles.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` documents `active_models=None` as meaning “all models active,” but the implementation uses `set(self.role_map.keys())` instead. See [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L516), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L579). After any subset reassignment, omitted models disappear from `role_map`, so a later `reassign(None)` will never reconsider them even though `_models` still contains them. A temporary subset can therefore become a permanent silent exclusion inside the role-assignment object.  
PROPOSED_FIX: When `active_models is None`, derive the default from `self._models`, not `self.role_map`, or require callers to pass `active_models` explicitly and reject `None`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` uses deterministic tie-breaking with `_tie_break_key`, but `reassign()` does not. It builds `remaining_ids` from a `set`, then chooses `best_col_id = max(col_scores, key=...)`, which ignores `_tie_break_key` entirely. See [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L462), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L526), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L558). If adjusted COL scores tie, winner selection falls back to insertion order from an unordered set, so reassignment can disagree with the documented deterministic rule even when the models’ tie-break fingerprints differ. This is distinct from the prior “exact full tie” finding: here the tie-break is omitted, not merely incomplete.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reassign from `ModelSpec` objects, not IDs, and select with a composite key like `(adjusted_score, _tie_break_key(model), model_id)`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` never validates that `model_id` values are unique. Because `capability_scores`, `role_map`, and `_failure_history` are keyed by `model_id`, later duplicates overwrite earlier ones, while `_models` still keeps both objects. See [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L454), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L469), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L496), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L536). That breaks the intended one-model/one-role mapping and makes later lookups order-dependent and ambiguous.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject duplicate `model_id`s at the start of `assign()` with a clear `ValueError`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: The failure layer can request `RecoveryAction.DOWNGRADE_ROLE` for repeated underperformance, and the tests assert that this action is returned, but no orchestration path actually applies that role downgrade. See [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2916), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3562), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3567), [bench/dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L524), [test_dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/tests/test_dynamic_management.py#L1014). This is especially broken for PM: repeated PM underperformance can request `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`, but `reassign()` always re-locks the PM, so the requested recovery is impossible.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either forbid `DOWNGRADE_ROLE` for PM and map it to another recovery, or make `process_round()` consume recovery actions explicitly and mutate role assignment accordingly for non-PM cases.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
